text:
jordan: Heads-up — ran a 4xA100 nsys + nvprof sweep on the KV-heavy chat workload and noticed an intermittent ~4-8ms bubble in the pipeline that lines up with an NCCL all-reduce gap. nvtx marks show the kernel-selector flipping strategies mid-request. full traces: https://redwood-artifacts/team/traces/2432109876 (nsys) and https://redwood-artifacts/team/traces/2432109876-nvprof.html

mira: ugh that sounds like the handshake/prefetch path. do you have a short timeline clip? can you paste the small nvprof summary?

jordan: pasted small nvprof snippet: ```
GPU 0: fused_attn_forward     3.2 ms  48%
GPU 0: kv_handshake_kernel    0.6 ms   9%
GPU 1: collective_allreduce   2.0 ms  30%
GPU 2: fused_attn_forward     3.1 ms  47%
...
(total wall: 12.4 ms, idle-gap ~6.1 ms between GPU1->GPU2 during allreduce)
```

samir: that idle-gap in the nvprof matches what I see in the nsys timeline — there's a ~5ms window where no compute kernels run but NCCL enqueued ops are waiting. nvtx shows a kernel-routing event right before that. my guess: kernel-selector decides to switch to a split-kernel (for long seq) which triggers a KV handshake that isn't overlapped with the collective path properly.

kelly: can you repro with KV prefetch disabled? try env var RH_DISABLE_KV_PREFETCH=1 and rerun a short trace. if gap goes away it's prefetch handshake ordering.

jordan: ran that — disabling prefetch reduced the bubble to ~1-2ms, and NCCL overlap looks cleaner. trace: https://redwood-artifacts/team/traces/2432109876-prefetch-off.nsys

mira: interesting. so the handshake introduces serialization between kernel launch sequences and NCCL progress. maybe our cudaStream ordering or stream priorities are causing the collective to wait. do we use the same stream for kv_handshake and the allreduce?

samir: currently kv_handshake runs on stream K and collectives run on comm stream C. but we enqueue a kernel-swap that touches the same CUDA graph region. if the kernel-selector emits a host callback to swap kernel variant, that could block enqueues until it completes. check for host-side synchronization in the selector.

jordan: grep'd selector log: ```
[selector] chose split_kernel variant for seq_len=1024; handshake_required=true; issuing host-sync barrier: true
```

kelly: there’s the culprit — host-sync barrier. we added that last quarter to ensure memory fences for the new quantized path but forgot to make it async-safe. quick fix: flip to use cudaEvent-based fence + streamWait so it doesn't stall host thread.

mira: before we change runtime, can we patch a temporary heuristic? if batch size < 12 && kv_prefetch=true then prefer fused_kernel (avoid split) — should reduce host-sync frequency. jordan, can you try a config patch and rerun?

jordan: patched batching heuristic locally, re-ran with prefetch on. bubble reduced to ~1.5-2.5ms in 90% of runs. two outliers remain where NVTX shows a host callback at enqueue time.

samir: can you capture the perfetto flame for one outlier and dump the CUDA API trace? need to inspect host-side callback stack. `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cuda_api,nvtx --sample=none -o out` should do it.

jordan: uploading perfetto slice + cuda_api dump: https://redwood-artifacts/team/traces/2432109876-outlier-perfetto.trace

kelly: stack shows `std::mutex` lock in selector path — oof. that explains the host callback. we need lock-free state transition or move that path to a background thread that issues async ops.

mira: short-term: add a fast-path that avoids taking the selector mutex for warmup handshakes (read-mostly case). long-term: redesign selector to be lock-free with epoch-based updates. I'll add a ticket.

perf-bot: Perf regression alert — since patch x.y.z the 99p latency for chat-inference increased by 5% on multi-gpu KV-heavy workloads across canary runs. Related traces: 2432109876.

samir: filing a dedicated perf ticket linking traces and regression graph. priority=p1. tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml.

jordan: next steps I took: 1) pushed cheap heuristic fallback (batch<12) to avoid split_kernel; 2) created a selector task to rip out host-sync barrier; 3) captured additional outlier traces and annotated NVTX. I'll follow up with a PR for the mutex fast-path today.

kelly: thanks. also add a small e2e canary with RH_DISABLE_KV_PREFETCH=0 + new heuristic to ensure we didn't regress recall/quality. we want to keep perf but not break outputs.

mira: note for the ticket — include nsys timeline snippets, nvprof kernel tables, and the host-side cuda_api stacks. those three together convinced the perf team.

samir: reminder: when we change the selector, test on 2x, 4x, and 8x GPU configs — some issues only appear at >=4 because of collective pipelining.

jordan: agreed. I'll run matrix tomorrow and post consolidated traces. thanks all :thumbsup:

kelly: :thumbsup: and leave a note in the release notes about the heuristic toggles and env flags for debugging (RH_DISABLE_KV_PREFETCH, RH_SELECTOR_FORCE_FUSED).
